question.problem:
The flight times of a particular drone model are normally distributed with a mean of $35$ minutes and a standard deviation of $4$ minutes. What is the probability that a randomly selected drone flies more than $40.08$ minutes on a single charge? **Round your answer to two decimal places.**

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8749\,$ | $\,0.8770\,$ | $\,0.8790\,$ |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8944\,$ | $\,0.8962\,$ | $\,0.8980\,$ |
| $\,1.3\,$ | $\,0.9115\,$ | $\,0.9131\,$ | $\,0.9147\,$ |

The probability that a randomly selected drone flies more than $40.08$ minutes on a single charge is approximately
{{field-1}}.
